newsitem.title: UK: S&P may cut Pearson senior debt, affirms CP.
newsitem.headline: S&P may cut Pearson senior debt, affirms CP.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it placed its A plus senior debt ratings of Pearson Plc and related entities on CreditWatch with negative implications.

This followed Pearson's announcement on Monday that, through its Penguin division, the company intended to acquire U.S.-based book publisher Putnam Berkley Group from MCA Inc. for $336 million in cash, S&P said.
"At the same time, Standard & Poor's affirms Pearson Inc.'s A1 commercial paper rating," it said in a statement.

"The CreditWatch placement reflects the negative financial impact of the proposed transaction, in light of Pearson's already weakened operating results over the past 18 months due to restructuring charges and the continuing integration of other acquisitions," S&P said.
It said it believed the proposed acquisition will enhance Pearson's already strong position in book publishing.
"Putnam Berkley Group is the seventh-largest trade book publisher in the United States. Post- acquisition, Penguin will rank as the third-largest U.S. trade book publisher," it said.
S&P said it will shortly meet with management to ascertain the specific impact of the proposed acquisition on Pearson's business and financial profile, before making a final rating determination.
